question: How is batch release performing this month?

tool_calls.query: SELECT AVG(cycle_d), AVG(rft), AVG(ontime), ... FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-08' AND month <= '2026-08' ; SELECT same KPIs FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-07' AND month <= '2026-07'
SELECT AVG(cycle_d), AVG(rft), AVG(ontime), ... FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-09' AND month <= '2026-09'

answer.text: Latest complete month (2026-08, 79 batches released): mean release cycle 16.4 d against a product-weighted target of 13.7 d; 25% released within target; right first time 49%.
Versus 2026-07 the mean cycle changed by +1.9 d and right first time by -16.5 points.
September is shown as provisional: 15 of 46 batches completed in 2026-09 have no usage decision yet, so its average is biased towards fast batches (right-censoring).

question: Why did performance deteriorate in August?

tool_calls.query: SELECT AVG(seg_documentation), AVG(seg_qc), AVG(seg_deviation), AVG(seg_qa_stage), AVG(seg_approval) FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-08' AND month <= '2026-08' ; SELECT same segments FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-07' AND month <= '2026-07'
SELECT exc_event, COUNT(*), AVG(cycle_d) FROM cases WHERE closed AND exc_event <> '' GROUP BY exc_event

events.title: Excipient lot quarantined by supplier notification
HVAC excursion in Grade B filling area

answer.text: Mean cycle went from 14.5 d (July) to 16.4 d (August). The largest increase is in "Deviation closure binding": +1.6 d per batch.
18 batches at Site B are linked to exceptional event EXC-2026-02 (HVAC excursion in Grade B filling area); their mean cycle is 24.5 d versus 14.8 d for unaffected Site B batches of the same month.
The August deterioration is mostly driven by the HVAC excursion through longer deviation closure. Test: exclude the event and recompute (next question).

question: Exclude the batches affected by the HVAC excursion. Is our performance actually improving?

tool_calls.query: SELECT AVG(cycle_d) FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-06' AND month <= '2026-08' ; SELECT AVG(cycle_d) FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-06' AND month <= '2026-08' AND exc_event NOT IN ('EXC-2026-02')

answer.text: Jun-Aug reported mean cycle 15.4 d; excluding the 18 affected batches it is 14.6 d, so the event added about 0.8 d to the reported average.
Underlying performance improved versus Mar-May (15.5 d, exceptional events excluded) by 0.9 d, but remains 1.3 d above the product-weighted target of 13.3 d.

question: Show me all similar exceptional events and exclude them from the last six months. Which KPI changed most?

tool_calls.query: SELECT exc_event, COUNT(*), AVG(cycle_d) FROM cases WHERE closed AND exc_event <> '' GROUP BY exc_event

events.title: Excipient lot quarantined by supplier notification
HVAC excursion in Grade B filling area

tool_calls.query: SELECT AVG(cycle_d) FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-03' AND month <= '2026-08' ; SELECT AVG(cycle_d) FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-03' AND month <= '2026-08' AND exc_event NOT IN ('EXC-2026-01', 'EXC-2026-02')

answer.text: The register holds 2 exceptional events: EXC-2026-01 Excipient lot quarantined by supplier notification at Site A (11 batches, mean cycle 18.1 d); EXC-2026-02 HVAC excursion in Grade B filling area at Site B (18 batches, mean cycle 24.5 d).
Excluding both from Mar-Aug removes 29 batches: mean cycle 15.4 d -> 15.0 d. The KPI that changed most (relative) is share of batches with a deviation: 23.5 -> 18.4.
Events are matched by an explicit reference on the deviation notification, not by text similarity; unlinked batches are never excluded silently.

question: Why is Site A slower than Site B on the same products?

tool_calls.query: SELECT material, site, AVG(...) FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-01' AND month <= '2026-05' AND exc_event NOT IN ('EXC-2026-01', 'EXC-2026-02') AND material IN (made at both sites) GROUP BY material, site

answer.text: Like-for-like, Jan-May, exceptional events excluded. Capsule 25 mg: Site A 11.1 d vs Site B 8.9 d (QA stage 4.4 vs 2.5 d; documentation rework 23% vs 8%); Injection 5 mL: Site A 23.2 d vs Site B 20.7 d (QA stage 4.2 vs 2.4 d; documentation rework 38% vs 14%).
Comparing only materials made at both sites removes the product-mix effect (Site B makes more sterile product with a 14-day sterility test).
Site A is slower mainly because batches queue longer for QA disposition review, and documentation is sent back more often. Both are addressable process drivers.

question: We introduced a quality-documentation pre-check at Site A on 1 June. Is it working?

tool_calls.query: SELECT kpi FROM cases WHERE closed AND site = '1100' AND mfg_complete BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-05-31' (pre) / BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-08-31' (post) AND exc_event = '' ; same for the other site (difference-in-differences)

intervention.title: Quality-documentation pre-check before QA batch record review

answer.text: Documentation rework at Site A: 30.7% before -> 9.4% after (-21.3 points; 95% CI -30.7 to -12.1; Fisher p < 0.001; n = 114 / 127).
Median QA review waiting 3.1 d -> 2.0 d (Mann-Whitney p < 0.001); median release cycle 12.1 d -> 10.5 d (p = 0.038).
Over the same windows Site B (no pre-check) changed by -0.1 points in documentation rework; the difference-in-differences is -21.1 points.
After the intervention, 49% of the remaining Site A cycle sits in "QC results binding".

The pre-check caused the reduction in documentation rework. The comparison site makes a common seasonal cause unlikely, but staffing or SOP changes in the same window would need to be ruled out by the process owner.

question: What do fast-release batches do differently?

tool_calls.query: SELECT cycle_d / target_d AS ratio, ... FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-01' AND month <= '2026-08' ; quartiles of ratio

answer.text: Fastest quartile (cycle <= 0.9 x target, n = 160) vs slowest quartile (>= 1.3 x target, n = 160): deviation 6% vs 49%; documentation rework 9% vs 29%; mean QA waiting 2.0 d vs 4.7 d; hand-offs 6.3 vs 8.1; expected-path conformance 81% vs 24%.
11% of slow batches went through two or more extra documentation-review cycles. Of batches more than 5 days over target, 65% had a deviation (vs 7% of batches released on time).
Deviation-closure latency and QA queueing appear to be the main contributors to slow release; association, not proven causation.

question: Which three issues should I address first?

tool_calls.query: SELECT segment means FROM cases WHERE closed AND month >= '2026-06' AND month <= '2026-08' ; internal best = min over site-quarter groups (n >= 15)

result.title: QA review waiting
result.recommendation: Daily QA release stand-up with a visible queue and a review-ready trigger from QC/MES

result.title: Deviation closure on the critical path
result.recommendation: Triage deviations at batch completion; fast lane for minor documentation deviations

result.title: QC result availability (oral solid)
result.recommendation: Prioritise QC test queue by release due date; review lab capacity at peaks

result.title: Usage-decision approval wait
result.recommendation: Release authorisations closer to QA review completion (e.g. extended QA release coverage)

result.title: Batch record documentation rework
result.recommendation: Right-first-time pre-check of batch records before QA review (replicate INT-01)

answer.text: Ranked by impact x frequency x confidence / effort (Jun-Aug, both sites): 1) QA review waiting: 0.5 d/batch above internal best (2.6 d vs 2.1 d), affects 50% of batches, score 0.11; 2) Deviation closure on the critical path: 1.6 d/batch above internal best (2.4 d vs 0.8 d), affects 14% of batches, score 0.07; 3) QC result availability (oral solid): 0.3 d/batch above internal best (4.5 d vs 4.2 d), affects 32% of batches, score 0.04.

Recommendations: Daily QA release stand-up with a visible queue and a review-ready trigger from QC/MES | Triage deviations at batch completion; fast lane for minor documentation deviations | Prioritise QC test queue by release due date; review lab capacity at peaks. Effort/risk weights are SME assumptions and should be confirmed with the process owner.
